title: 2 Chronicles 10
paragraphs: ¹ Rehoboam traveled to Shechem, where all Israel had gathered to crown him king. ² When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard the news — he was still in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon — he returned from Egypt. ³ The people sent for him, and he and all Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam. ⁴ "Your father made our yoke unbearable," they said. "Lighten the harsh labor and the heavy yoke he placed on us, and we will serve you." ⁵ Rehoboam answered, "Come back to me in three days." So the people left.

⁶ King Rehoboam consulted the elders who had served his father Solomon during his lifetime. "What is your advice?" he asked. "How should I answer these people?" ⁷ They said to him, "If you are good to these people and please them and speak kindly to them, they will be your servants forever." ⁸ But he rejected the advice of the elders and turned instead to the young men who had grown up with him and now served him. ⁹ "What is your advice?" he asked them. "How should we answer these people who are asking me to lighten the yoke my father put on them?" ¹⁰ The young men who had grown up with him replied, "Tell these people who said your father's yoke was too heavy — tell them this: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's waist.'"

¹¹ "Where my father burdened you with a heavy yoke, I will make it heavier still. Where my father beat you with whips, I will beat you with scorpions." ¹² So Jeroboam and all the people returned to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had ordered. ¹³ The king answered them harshly. King Rehoboam rejected the elders' advice ¹⁴ and spoke to the people as the young men had advised: "Where my father made your yoke heavy, I will add to it. Where my father beat you with whips, I will beat you with scorpions." ¹⁵ So the king did not listen to the people — this was the will of God, fulfilling what the LORD had spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.

¹⁶ When all Israel saw that the king refused to listen to them, the people answered the king: "What share do we have in David? We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse! Every man to his tent, Israel! Look after your own house, David!" So all Israel returned to their tents. ¹⁷ But Rehoboam still ruled over the Israelites who lived in the cities of Judah. ¹⁸ King Rehoboam sent out Hadoram, who was in charge of forced labor, but the Israelites stoned him to death. King Rehoboam barely managed to climb into his chariot and flee to Jerusalem. ¹⁹ And Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David to this day.
